source.title: Robust Learning with Frequency Domain Regularization

record.tranche_reason: Tests generalization performance and the train-test gap using a different explicit regularizer, but does not test the claim versions’ specified interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports same-dataset test accuracy under frequency-domain regularization and train/test accuracy curves. Corruption results in Table 2 concern transformed inputs and are excluded as out-of-distribution results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates learned frequency masks and their effects on accuracy and robustness. Its own results do not test V1–V8. Randomly dropping frequencies in R9 is not the classifier dropout intervention in V6; discussion of random-label fitting and sharpness summarizes prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: learned frequency masks identify useful frequency ranges and improve robustness on unseen data. The abstract additionally claims reduced generalization gaps and transfer without finetuning; the supplied results do not establish all these claims through clearly specified numerical comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: Uses learned frequency masks on convolution layers; the listed original studies concern other interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test accuracies vary with the combination of normalization, augmentation, weight decay, random crop, and random drop.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports LeNet CIFAR-10 test accuracies for baseline, augmentation, normalization, weight decay, and learned frequency-mask configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned frequency masks can improve test accuracy relative to some baseline training configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 plots training accuracy, test accuracy, and their gap for original, proposed-method, and sketch training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frequency-domain regularization changes training and test performance and their gap.

record.problems: Figure 2 provides no extractable numeric values; Table 1 is flattened and supplies no uncertainty estimates. The paper does not report random-label fitting.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports clean and corruption accuracies for natural, Gaussian, adversarial, and proposed training, but these are transformed-input robustness results, outside the same-distribution generalization versions. Table 3 reports mask percentages, not an outcome on the claim.

untested.parts: No own random-label fitting experiment or natural-versus-random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No optimizer comparison; all models use momentum SGD.
No reported ordinary-dropout comparison, dropout-rate sweep, small-data comparison, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization-gap measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1's flattened values match the recorded ordering. Its caption mentions dropout variants, but no corresponding ordinary-dropout results appear. Table 2 includes clean-image accuracy as well as corruption accuracy, so calling the entire table transformed-input results is inaccurate; neither portion bears on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy; no random-label control.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of gap measures.
